The maximum period permissible for late registration due to medical shall not be more

than two (02) calendar weeks counted from the specified date of Registration announced by the University.
- **Course Add/Drop** — Students may add or drop Courses after consulting the concerned Faculty Advisor [Mentor] and submit a request for add or drop to the concerned Program Chair/Dean of Schools within two weeks of the commencement of the classes as notified in the Academic Calendar or notifications issued by the University to this effect.

[SOP › 1. Course Registration]
- **Audit Course Registration** — A student who desires to register to Audit a Course shall consult their Faculty Advisor (Mentor) and seek approval of the concerned Course Instructor. Registration to Audit a Course shall be permitted after approval by the concerned Program Chair. The student does not earn credits for Audited Course.

[SOP › 2. Student Attendance]
- Course wise attendance can be checked on Digii Portal on a daily basis. Attendance report will be shared with the parents and students twice per semester by the Office of the Registrar.
- For any concern regarding the attendance, student to contact the respective faculty members.
- For the End-Term Examination, the attendance recorded on Digii will be considered as FINAL.
- To appear for end semester examination, the attendance requirement shall be a minimum of seventy five percent (75%) of the classes actually conducted in every Course the student has registered for in the Academic Term.
- Further, (a) if a student / family member suffers serious medical exigencies of hospitalization, trauma or contagious disease only (for the student / family member[s]) the concerned student may submit the leave request together with the documents to the Faculty Advisor for recommendation to the Program Chair. The approved / signed medical applications along with specified documents to be submitted by the student on the day of rejoining to the concern department and raise a medical leave request on Digii portal by uploading all the documents. Failing which leave on medical grounds will not be accepted. The medical certificate will be considered only for the entire day not for specific class/ hours.

[SOP › 2. Student Attendance]
- (b) if a student represents the State / National / International Events / Competitions, the concerned student may submit the

letter to the Director, Campus Life and Faculty Advisor for recommendation to the Program Chair.
- Such students (a & b) will be given relaxation in attendance requirement (in the Course(s) where there is a shortage) for the concerned period of absence. However, the minimum requirement of attendance will be sixty five percent (65%) of the classes actually conducted in every Course the student has registered for in the Academic Term.
- The student shall not be eligible for this special provision if she/he fails to produce authentic certificates and relevant documents, including fitness certificate (in the case of Medical), on the day of rejoining the classes.

[SOP › 3. Change of Program]
- Student may seek transfer from one Program to another Program before the commencement of the registration for the Second Year with the due approval of the existing and the new Program Chair, subject to the eligibility criteria and provisions of the academic regulations.
- Student to submit request letter signed by parents to the existing Program Chair and after obtaining the signature, the same letter to be submitted to the Office of the Registrar for further process.
- The "Credit Transfer Equivalence Committee" shall review the application of the student for Program change and transfer of credits. This committee shall submit its recommendations to the office of the Registrar for approval.
- On no account a transfer from one Program to another will be allowed beyond the stipulated period.

[SOP › 4. Summer Term Registration]
- The Summer Term is an additional Academic Term that may be offered during the summer break June-July.
- A limited number of Courses may be offered in the Summer Term. A student cannot demand for a specific Course to be offered.
- A student may re-register for the Course(s) if offered, by paying the prescribed fees and completing the course registration process on or before the last date for Registration as specified in the Academic Calendar. No late registration shall be permitted.
- The Attendance requirement as per Academic Regulation shall be applicable to all students registering for Course(s) in the Summer Term.

[SOP › 5. University Annual Fee]
- The student shall remit the Annual University Fee as prescribed by the University for the concerned Program of study and clear

any other dues, to get eligible for Course registration every semester.
- Students with outstanding fees will not be permitted to appear for the semester-end examination.

[SOP › 6. Digii Account]
- Digii is a comprehensive software platform designed to streamline and manage various academic functions within the institution.
- Students will be provided with a Digii User ID and Password to log in to Digii Portal.
- Student to update the personal and academic details to complete the admission process.
- Once logged in, students will have access to a wide range of academic services, including: Course Registration, Cohort and Batch Details, Attendance Records, Bonafide Certificate Requests, Examination Details, Medical Leave ….
- For any issues related to Digii, students should contact the Office of the Registrar for assistance.

[SOP › 7. Bonafide Certificate]
**Educational Loan:**
- The student must email to the Accounts Department requesting for the fee structure. The Office of the Registrar must be kept in the email loop.
- Simultaneously, the student must raise a Bonafide Certificate request through Digii – Campus Help Centre, clearly mentioning the reason (required for an educational loan).

**Internship:**
- The student must email the Program Chair requesting approval for the internship. The email should include all relevant details, such as: (Company Name, Internship Duration, Start Date, End Date, Any other relevant internship details)
- The Office of the Registrar must be kept in the email loop. Simultaneously, the student must raise a Bonafide Certificate request through Digii – Campus Help Centre, clearly mentioning the reason (required for an internship).

**Scholarship / Passport:**
- The student must raise a Bonafide Certificate request through Digii – Campus Help Centre clearly mentioning the reason.

The Bonafide Certificate will be issued on Digii within 24 hours of submitting the request.

[SOP › 8. Scholarship]
- Students seeking support or information regarding scholarships shall contact the Office of the Registrar.

[SOP › 9. Grievance]
- Students can submit their grievances online.
- Send your grievance to studentgrievance@vidyashilp.edu.in Email ID only.
- Submit through the official grievance form by clicking the link below: https://vidyashilp.edu.in/Student_Grievance/

[SOP › 10. General]
To ensure a seamless university experience, all students are required to adhere to the following guidelines:
- Students must wear the ID Card compulsory at all times while on campus.
- **Safety of equipment in the classroom:** Utilize upgraded classroom / lab facilities such as Interactive Display Panels (IDP), chairs, and tables responsibly. Damages caused by intentional or negligent behaviour will have consequences.
- **Exercise mindfulness during meals:** Eat in designated spaces, especially in the cafeteria. Avoid eating in classrooms / Lab to maintain a conducive learning environment.
- **Use of internet services:** University wi-fi is exclusively for academic use. Using wi-fi other than academic purpose and video streaming are prohibited. Violations will be viewed seriously.
- **Maintain campus cleanliness:** Do not litter. CCTV cameras monitor for compliance and violations will result in consequences.
- **Respect shared spaces:** Sofas at reception are for guests. Use alternative seating in the lawn or cafeteria.
- **Infirmary usage:** Visit the infirmary if you are unwell.

[SOP › 11. Vehicle and Parking Guidelines]
- **Vehicle access limitations:** Vehicles are strictly not permitted to drive beyond the designated parking point. Exceptions are made only for emergencies (medical issues or disability).
- **Speed limit enforcement:** Vehicle speed within the campus is limited to 20 kmph to ensure safety for all.
- **Triple riding prohibition:** Triple riding on two-wheelers is strictly not allowed.

- Wearing a helmet is mandatory for two-wheeler riders.
- **Reception access:** Only vehicles driven by parents / guardians or authorized drivers may drive till the reception.
- **Carpool/bike pool protocol:** Vehicles used for student carpooling or bike pooling must stop at the parking point. Students must walk from there; vehicles are not permitted to drop off students at Reception and then park.
- **Parking restrictions:** Vehicles are not allowed to park at Reception or in front of the Design Studio. Parking is permitted only in the designated parking areas.

**General communication:** Students are advised to regularly check their emails inbox for important University communication / circular from registrar.office@vidyashilp.edu.in or concern departments. Timely responses and attention to these communications are essential to avoid missing important information.

text: Data/policy conflict: Minimum attendance: 75% (Academic Regulations, SOP) vs 80% (Code of Conduct). Academic Regulations clause 7.2 (Student Handbook, printed p.21) and SOP section 2 (p.2) set the minimum attendance to appear for end-semester examinations at 75% of classes conducted in every course (relaxable to no less than 65% for documented medical exigencies or approved State/National/International events, clauses 7.3-7.4 / SOP section 2). The Code of Conduct clause 4.5 in the same Handbook (Section IV, printed p.45) says 'Students must comply with the attendance requirement of 80%'. No precedence rule between these sections is stated in the provided documents; the Academic Regulations (amended 29 July 2025) and the SOP (17 Aug 2026) agree on 75% for exam eligibility.
citation: Student Handbook §7.2 (Academic Regulations), p.21; SOP §2 Student Attendance, p.2; Student Handbook Code of Conduct §4.5, p.45

text: Data/policy conflict: Late registration: 'not permitted' vs 'up to one week'. SOP section 1 ('Late Registration', p.1) states 'No late registration shall be permitted' except for medical exigencies or competitions/events (maximum two calendar weeks for medical cases). The same SOP section ('Course Registration Deadline', p.1) says the maximum permissible period for late registration is one calendar week, and Handbook clause 2.7 (printed p.16) permits late registration for any other reason for up to one calendar week with a late fee. The documents do not reconcile the 'not permitted' wording with the one-week allowance.
